Genetic & developmental syndromes 8

Treacher Collins

mandibulofacial dysostosis
TCOF1 · POLR1C · POLR1D

Symmetric deficiency of the zygoma & mandible, downslanting palpebral fissures, coloboma, ear anomalies.

Ortho: Severe mandibular deficiency → Class II, anterior open bite, airway compromise. 5

Crouzon

craniofacial dysostosis
FGFR2 & FGFR3 (chr 10)

Premature coronal-suture fusion, midface hypoplasia, exorbitism (an illusion from the deficient midface).

Ortho: Maxillary deficiency → Class III, crowding, airway/OSA risk. 5

Apert

acrocephalosyndactyly
FGFR2

Crouzon-like synostosis PLUS syndactyly of hands & feet; severe midface hypoplasia.

Ortho: Maxillary deficiency, Class III, very crowded high-arched palate. 5

Achondroplasia

autosomal dominant
FGFR3 (auto. dominant)

Deficient endochondral cranial-base growth → midface deficiency; normal-size mandible.

Ortho: Relative mandibular prognathism → skeletal Class III. 5

Ectodermal dysplasia

hypohidrotic (X-linked)
ectodermal genes

Thin sparse hair, absent sweat glands, conical teeth, oligodontia/anodontia.

Ortho: Most likely cause when many teeth are congenitally missing; reduced vertical dimension. 5

Cleidocranial dysplasia

RUNX2 / CBFA1
RUNX2 (CBFA1)

Absent/hypoplastic clavicles, frontal bossing, delayed suture closure.

Ortho: Delayed eruption, multiple supernumeraries, retained primary teeth, pseudo-anodontia. 35

Down syndrome

trisomy 21
trisomy 21

Midface deficiency, macroglossia, hypotonia, brachycephaly.

Ortho: Class III tendency, anterior open bite, hypodontia, delayed eruption, periodontal risk. 25

Craniofacial microsomia

hemifacial microsomia
developmental (1st/2nd arch)

Deficient ramus/condyle, microtia, soft-tissue & facial asymmetry (often unilateral).

Ortho: Unilateral mandibular deficiency → occlusal cant, midline shift. 5

Clefts & craniosynostosis 3

Cleft lip & palate

≈1/700 (varies by ethnicity)
multifactorial

Failure of fusion of facial/palatal processes; uni- or bilateral, complete or incomplete.

Ortho: Maxillary deficiency (esp. after repair), missing/malformed lateral incisor, crossbites; needs NAM, grafting, team care. 57

Craniosynostosis

1/2200 · 25% syndromic
FGFR1/2/3 · TWIST1

Premature cranial-suture fusion distorts skull shape; ideal surgical release 3–9 months.

Ortho: Skull/orbital distortion; midface effects in syndromic forms. 5

Pierre Robin

a SEQUENCE, not a syndrome
± Stickler syndrome

Micrognathia → glossoptosis → U-shaped cleft palate + airway obstruction at birth.

Ortho: Small mandible may 'catch up'; early airway management is the priority. 5

Acquired & asymmetry causes 9

Fetal alcohol syndrome

teratogen: alcohol
ethanol, 1st trimester

Central midface deficiency, short palpebral fissures, smooth philtrum, developmental delay.

Ortho: Midface deficiency → Class III tendency. 5

Childhood condylar fracture

acquired
trauma

Damage to the condylar growth site → asymmetric mandibular deficiency; ankylosis risk.

Ortho: Unilateral mandibular deficiency, chin deviation to the affected side. 5

Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis

TMJ involvement
autoimmune

Bilateral condylar resorption → progressive mandibular deficiency ('bird face').

Ortho: Retrognathia, anterior open bite, steep mandibular plane. 5

Masseter / motor-nerve deficiency

muscle agenesis
muscle / nerve loss

Underdevelopment of bone where muscle attachment/function is missing.

Ortho: Asymmetric facial deficiency on the affected side. 5

Torticollis

SCM contracture
muscle contracture

Tonic neck-muscle contraction twists the head → restricted growth.

Ortho: Facial asymmetry / plagiocephaly. 5

Decreased muscle activity

e.g. muscular dystrophy
weak musculature

Low occlusal/masticatory force → posterior over-eruption.

Ortho: Long lower face, anterior open bite. 5

Hemimandibular hyperplasia

~85% female
condylar overgrowth

Gradual unilateral mandibular overgrowth.

Ortho: Chin deviates to the OPPOSITE side, occlusal canting; treat after growth. 5

Acromegaly

GH excess
pituitary GH excess

Adult mandibular overgrowth, enlarged hands/feet/brow.

Ortho: Adult skeletal Class III with spacing. 5

X-ray

Dilaceration

trauma to developing tooth
trauma

Sharp angulation of the crown/root after the developing tooth is displaced.

Ortho: Eruption failure / difficult alignment; seen on the radiograph. 5

People, growth science & theories 9

Melvin MossFunctional matrix theory — bones grow in response to their functional soft-tissue matrices. 2
Donald EnlowSurface remodeling, the “V principle,” and the counterpart principle of facial growth. 24
Arne BjörkMetallic-implant studies that revealed true (internal) jaw rotation. 24
Richard ScammonThe four tissue growth curves (neural, general, lymphoid, genital). 2
Moorrees & ChadhaStages of tooth formation used for dental age. 3
Edward ReitanClassic histology of PDL/tissue reaction to orthodontic force. 8
Harold FrostRegional Acceleratory Phenomenon (RAP) — basis of accelerated tooth movement. 8
Pavlov · Skinner · Thorndike · PiagetClassical/operant conditioning & cognitive-development models of child behavior. 2
